question: May experimental Claws register arbitrary stdio MCP commands and reuse global named MCP declarations, or must they use a host-authorized broker/allowlist with explicitly authorized shared resources?
rationale: This is a persistent execution and cross-role ownership contract; code review cannot safely choose the intended trust boundary without maintainer direction.

options.title: Require brokered and scoped MCP ownership
options.body: Require a host-approved command path or allowlist and make shared global MCP declarations an explicit authorized resource before this lifecycle feature can merge.

options.title: Accept global manifest authority
options.body: Document that enabling experimental Claws authorizes arbitrary manifest-provided stdio commands and global exact-declaration sharing, with the associated operator risk.

options.title: Defer MCP mutation
options.body: Keep Claw MCP support read-only or omit it until the lifecycle RFC defines the execution and resource-scoping contract.

recommendation.title: Require brokered and scoped MCP ownership
recommendation.body: Require a host-approved command path or allowlist and make shared global MCP declarations an explicit authorized resource before this lifecycle feature can merge.
